how.title: How it works
how.sub: First the structure, then the rubric, and finally the cycle. At every step, the school reviews, adjusts and decides.

steps.title: Set up the org chart and roles
steps.desc: Load your school's structure and link each position to a catalog role. The AI suggests the best fit and explains why, and you confirm it or pick another.

steps.desc: Every role gets a rubric with curated questions, organised by framework and area and tied to Chilean regulation. The AI accompanies you through the selection and helps with any doubts along the way; adjust whatever you want before publishing.

steps.title: Launch the 360° cycle and read the results
steps.desc: Decide how much each perspective weighs and which stages the process goes through, launch it and, at the close, get achievement by domain with an improvement suggestion for each person.

faq.title: FAQ
faq.sub: What school boards, principals and HR teams ask us most.

items.q: Does it work for education assistants?
items.a: Yes. Eleva evaluates every role in the school: teachers, leadership, education assistants, inclusion teams (PIE), administrative staff and management. The catalog covers every role, with its name, aliases and gender variants.

The rubric follows Eleva's methodology and is always a proposal, never an imposition: you review the questions, adjust dimensions and weights, and approve it before launching the process. Every process freezes its configuration when it is generated, so past cycles stay untouched.

items.q: What does the AI do, and what does the school decide?
items.a: The AI does not invent content: it guides your team through Eleva's methodology. It points you to the catalog role that matches each position and explains why, walks you through assembling the rubric from the curated bank, clears up doubts during the process and, at the end, organises the improvement suggestions by domain. The decisions — the role, the rubric, the weights and the result — always belong to the school.

items.q: How does it align with Chilean regulation?
items.a: Every question in the bank declares the regulation and frameworks it evaluates: Ley 21.643 (Ley Karin), Ley 20.903 on the teaching career, the Framework for Good School Leadership (MBDLE), Ley 21.719 on personal data protection, Ley 20.536 on school violence and the child protection laws, among others. Each role's rubric shows what it aligns to.

items.q: Which perspectives and stages does the 360° have?
items.a: The 360° looks at each person from four perspectives: their self-assessment, their manager's view, their direct reports' and their peers', with the weights you define (together they add up to 100). The process goes through six stages: in preparation, started, in feedback, feedback answered, finalized and closed.

items.q: Does it work for a board running several schools?
items.a: Yes. Central configuration sets the default stages and values for the whole network, and each school can override them on its own stages page.
